title: normalize v1/chat param handshake and toolcall metadata to improve streaming stability
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Improve /v1/chat.completions parameter negotiation and streaming handshake to reduce dropped tool/function calls and stabilize logprob/stop framing across adapters.
description: Context: production traffic showed intermittent stream termination when client params (roles/stop/logprobs) and tool-call metadata were negotiated between the OpenAI v1 adapter and the runtime. This manifested as truncated function call envelopes and missing logprobs on replayed tokens. Motivation: make Redwood's OpenAI-compatible v1/chat surface resilient to mixed client shapes and partially-specified tool metadata so hosted customers and Dedicated tenants get consistent streaming semantics. Changes: 1) added an explicit handshake step in the adapter that canonicalizes incoming v1 parameters (role aliases, stop as string|array, logprobs enum) into the runtime's internal CallSpec; 2) introduce a compact toolcall metadata envelope emitted as the first streaming event for function-invocation flows so downstream stream decoders can reconcile call boundaries even with upstream backpressure; 3) implemented idempotent resume frames that include truncated-kv offsets to allow safe resume/replay during intermittent connection drops; 4) tightened stop/logprobs framing rules so logprob frames are only emitted after a complete token frame and are associated by token offset to avoid misalignment; 5) added integration tests and fuzz harness for mixed role/stop shapes. Backwards compatibility: adapter accepts all legacy v1 shapes and prefers normalized canonical form when echoing back in structured responses. See linked Linear tasks ENG-4281 and ENG-4307 for acceptance criteria. Checklist: - [x] canonicalize params (roles, stop, logprobs) - [x] emit toolcall metadata envelope on stream start for tool flows - [x] resume frames with kv offset - [x] add integration tests and CI job - [x] add docs snippet under docs/openai_v1_handshake.md Related: incident INT-2142 (hotfix rollback during network blips).
